rail_guard.text: Kent Station. Trains to every Irish station you have visited. Cork people call themselves the real capital. The trains, with a straight face, go along with it.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

then.text: Best market in the world, you say? Don't tell the Queen. She once stopped at this very stall, in 2011, and I swear she laughed at my joke.
Both stamps? Grand. You've tasted the lot. A true Corkonian, or at least a lodger.
Here, a pasty for the road. I don't know why a fishmonger has pasties. It's a long story, and it involves a Cornish aunt.

else.text: One stamp down. The spiced-beef man, round the corner, still needs to give you his.
Two stalls to taste, and I'll stamp the card: the baker and the spiced-beef man, in the Market. Stamp the card, bring it back.
The English Market! Trading since 1788. That's when the first stalls went up, the roof came on later, and the name stuck, though everything in here is as Cork as a pint of Murphy's.
Fresh off the boat this morning. Which boat? The boat. Don't ask for details, it's a trade secret.
Tell you what: there's a market trail. Taste the baker's and the spiced-beef man's, collect their stamps, and I'll give you a feed for the road.

then.text: Fog over Shandon. You can't see the salmon, but you'll hear the bells, girl. Guaranteed.
Wind's spinning the golden salmon like a top. He'll be dizzy by teatime.

bell_ringer.text: {greeting} You can ring the Shandon bells yourself. There's a tune sheet, and a lot of enthusiasm. The tune will be recognisable. Possibly.
There's a golden salmon on top of the tower, as the weathervane. Cork's had a long relationship with fish.

then.text: Rain in Cork? Sure, it's a Tuesday. Or a Wednesday. Or any day ending in Y, like.
Sun out over Cork! The whole city is mighty today, boy. Mighty altogether.
Lovely evening, like. The lights on the river would make you proud to be a Rebel.

rebel_local.text: We call ourselves 'Rebels', in Cork. It's the Rebel County. It's not a very dangerous thing. Mostly we rebel against other counties' accents.
Cork has its own sing-song accent, its own words, and a lot of pride in both. It's very affectionate. You'll find yourself copying it by teatime.

then.text: Rain? I'm going in the river anyway. Can't get wetter than wet, can you?
Too choppy for a swim today. The swans have gone home and so should I.
Dawn swim's the best one. The Lee's all mist and swans and nobody watching.

lee_swimmer.text: {greeting} The Lee splits in two and runs round both sides of the city centre, and people swim in both. It's quite the commute. Mind the swans, they know where the bread is.
Cork Harbour, at the end of the river, is one of the biggest natural harbours in the world. A sailor's dream. A swimmer's disagreement.

then.text: Fog this morning. I can hear the trains before I see them, which makes it a game.
First train of the day! Number one on the list. Twelve more and I've matched yesterday.

kent_stationman.text: Kent Station's named for Thomas Kent, a Cork man executed after the 1916 Rising. It used to be called Glanmire Road. People still call it that, to be safe.
I'm collecting every train that comes through. So far it's been thirteen. I'm told that's a low number for a day.

market_baker.text: Soda bread, still warm. Brown and white. The brown's for people who've had a stressful week.
A stamp for your card? Here you go. A bit of flour on it. That's a feature.

market_spice.text: Spiced beef. You cure it for two weeks and it's gone by Christmas Eve. Drisheen, tripe, a bit of everything, mostly the good stuff.
A stamp for the trail? Take it, and take a slice. If you don't like it, tell me, and I'll pretend I didn't hear.

cork_astronomer.text: There's an observatory at Blackrock Castle, down the river. A castle full of telescopes. Only in Cork.
Clear night, for once! I'd put the kettle on, but I'll miss Jupiter.
The stars over the harbour are mighty tonight, like. Look up, go on.

cork_night_nurse.text: Off to the hospital for the night shift. Twelve hours, one flask, and a fierce amount of biscuits.
The city's lovely and quiet at this hour. Just me and the gulls arguing.
Mind yourself going home, like. Get a good sleep in for me.

cork_roadbowler.text: Down the lane past the quays, the road is shut for the afternoon. Bring an iron bowl and a good eye for a bend.
